notes.summary: Two approximation inferences fail: common −∞ values defeat the displayed BJ4.6 strict-shift argument, and changing divisor coefficients can make a divided net increase. Ample compactness repairs the required divisor division.
notes.detailedSummary: These are counterexamples to displayed proof steps, not disproofs of the published theorems. The reconstruction uses real-valued continuous approximants on the fixed actual ample bundle and normalized ample compactness instead of divided-net monotonicity. Homogeneous decomposition and ample EP then recover the full reference-dominated cone on the projective source.
notes.text:
Assume k is algebraically closed, trivially valued, characteristic zero, Y is smooth integral projective, and actual rational data satisfy L_Y=A+D with A ample and D effective. Put σ=log|s_D|. The exact ample P16.1 grant is used only on Y,A.

The supplied BJ4.6 proof asserts strict inequality after positive constant shifts and then strict negativity of an exponential difference everywhere. On K=[0,1], let g(x)=log x, with log0=−∞, and f_j(x)=log(x+1/j). These are extended-valued continuous functions and f_j decreases to g. At zero, f_j+ε cannot lie below g+ε₀ for any finite constants. An outer pair having one exact inner function g and one inner approximating family f_j has no upper triple in the displayed preorder. The exponential limit there is zero. This invalidates that directedness argument; it does not disprove the flattening theorem.

There is also an actual geometric counterexample to the divided-net monotonicity inference in BJ6.21. On Y=P¹, take D a point and A=O(1). For i≥2 set h_i=(1−i⁻²)σ, L_i=A+(1−i⁻²)D, and t_i=1−i⁻¹. Multiplication by powers of s_D and a generating system on a clearing power of A gives genuine homogeneous section maxima h_i in the actual L_i. They decrease to σ and satisfy h_i≤t_iσ. But r_i=h_i−t_iσ=(i⁻¹−i⁻²)σ increases wherever σ<0. Both required class and coefficient limits hold. At σ=−1, the first divided values are −1/4, −2/9, −3/16.

The repair is as follows. For homogeneous h≤σ, BJ6.17 gives decreasing homogeneous section approximants h_i in L_i with classes tending to A+D. Compactness of {σ=−1} permits rational t_i→1 with sup h_i≤−t_i there. Homogeneity gives h_i≤t_iσ on divisorial valuations; BJ4.22 extends it everywhere. BJ2.23 literally divides sections, producing genuine r_i in L_i−t_iD. Choose rational c_i>1 tending to one so c_iA−c₁(L_i−t_iD) is ample. Then r_i/c_i is genuine A-psh with supremum zero. Granted ample compactness supplies a subnet limit r having divisorial values h−σ. Genuine addition and divisorial determination imply h=σ+r everywhere. No decreasing assertion for r_i is needed.

For general v≤σ+C, BJ6.24 gives v=sup_λ(ĥv_λ+λ). Scaling removes the constant from domination of each homogeneous component. Apply the repair to obtain ĥv_λ=σ+r_λ. The family r_λ+λ is uniformly upper bounded; ample EP gives its usc supremum r. BJ5.6 preserves divisorial values, and divisorial determination gives v=σ+r everywhere. Thus the entire reference-dominated genuine cone on Y is σ+PSH(Y,A), with unique quotient. The case D=0 is immediate.

Fixed actual A approximation uses the exact granted real-valued continuous ample section nets, avoiding arbitrary extended-valued flattening. notes.detailedSummary: Chow plus resolution provides a smooth projective birational source above every smooth integral proper carrier. An actual big Cartier bundle exists on the original carrier, and every retained big rational L admits an actual pullback decomposition A+D. Stacks0BFP(4) excludes quasi-finite points over the bad image; antiample restrictions force whole-fiber vanishing. Analytic and baseline algebraic primary-source audits remain explicitly incomplete.
notes.text:
Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued, characteristic zero, and X smooth integral proper of dimension n≥1. Stacks0200/0201 provides a proper birational quasi-projective refinement with integral dense closure. Since X is proper, its immersion into projective space is closed. Temkin0904.1592v2 Theorem1.2.1 supplies a finite projective blowup resolution Y, integral smooth projective. Retain π:Y→X. Stacks0AY8 applies to the normal base with generic fiber Spec k(X), proving π_*O_Y=O_X and geometrically connected fibers.

Choose a very ample effective H on Y avoiding the finitely many exceptional prime divisors; global generation and infinitude of k permit this. B=π_*H is effective Cartier on smooth X. Stacks0BFP gives isomorphism at codimension-one points, so π*B=H+E with E effective exceptional. Projection formula identifies original sections, and multiplication by s_E^m embeds H⁰(Y,mH) in H⁰(X,mB). Ample growth proves that B is an actual big original bundle. A direct growth argument chooses n algebraically independent rational functions, clears their poles by a common section of qH, and obtains binomial(m+n,n) independent monomial sections of mqH. No ample bundle on X is asserted.

For ANY retained big rational L, section identification makes π*L big. Clear denominators to F on Y. Choose an effective very ample Cartier hyperplane T without assuming reducedness or irreducibility. On T, a sufficiently positive ample twist N−F|T is globally generated. A section avoiding the finitely many associated points gives injections F^m|T→N^m. Stacks0B5T and0BEM yield h⁰(T,N^m)=O(m^(n−1)). Big growth and the restriction exact sequence produce a nonzero section of mF−M, where M defines T. Dividing its effective divisor and M by m and the clearing denominator gives an actual identity π*L=A+D, A ample and D effective. Choices are fixed before a target; no Bertini, finite generation or countability is used.

Let B_π be the nonisomorphism image. Stacks0BFP(4) excludes every quasi-finite point above B_π over normal X. Every reduced geometric fiber component there has positive dimension. On such a component F, π*L is trivial and O(mD)|F=(−mA)|F is antiample. A nonzero antiample section would, by taking powers, inject sections of a sufficiently large very ample positive power into H⁰(F,O), contradicting its one-dimensional space of constants. Hence s_D vanishes on the entire geometric fiber; nilpotents introduce no additional analytic points.

Put P=π(|D|). It contains B_π. Above B_π every fiber is contained in D; outside B_π every fiber is a singleton. Therefore π⁻¹(P)=|D| set-theoretically. Conditional on the standard proper-analytic surjectivity facts, π⁻¹(P^an)=|D|^an and the complements are analytically isomorphic. This saturation is essential for taking maxima of polar tests over entire fibers.

notes.summary: An explicit actual ample E¹ pole excludes the entire saturated polar image through finite relative dual energy. A Radon inverse lemma then proves the intrinsic all-E¹ quotient-integrability characterization, conditional on analytic descent.
notes.detailedSummary: The original quotient is the maximum of the uniquely determined genuine ample potential over the entire compact fiber. It need not be psh or affine on bad fibers. The polar test uses an actual section and exponent 1/(n+2). The Radon inverse proof uses Riesz representation, cutoffs and inner regularity without metrizability, countable exhaustion or point selection. The exact relative mass is Aⁿ; integrability concerns the relative quotient rather than the absolute singular metric.
notes.text:
Use the retained geometry and saturated polar image P from n2, the division repair from n1, and assume the standard compact proper analytic quotient/center facts. For the whole reference-dominated original-section cone, Q(u) is the unique genuine potential in PSH(Y,A) satisfying π*u=σ+Q(u). It is determined off D and by divisorial determination. Define q_u(x)=max_{π(y)=x}Q(u)(y), over the entire compact fiber. Finite upper-level sets are images of compact upper-level sets, so q_u is usc and Borel. No psh or affine property is assumed on bad fibers. Nested compact upper-level sets prove that fiber maxima commute with decreasing genuine quotient nets.

Choose an actual nonzero section s of a clearing power mA vanishing on D, using positive-twist generation of its ideal. Put a=m⁻¹log|s|≤0, sup a=0, and α=1/(n+2). The convex increasing function χ(t)=−(−t)^α for t≤−1, continued with slope α on [−1,0], has slopes in [0,1]. BJ4.10 gives w=1−(1−a)^α as genuine A-psh, normalized to zero and −∞ on D. BJ7.47 gives Cap{w≤−t}≤n/((t+1)^(1/α)−1). Its sufficient energy integral, retaining the factor tⁿ, has tail O(t⁻²). Thus w is an ACTUAL E¹(Y,A) potential. Saturation π⁻¹(P)=D implies q_{F(w)}=−∞ on every point of P.

Define E_M(F(ψ))=E_raw,A(ψ) and, for an original Radon measure μ of mass V=Aⁿ, D_M(μ)=sup_u(E_M(u)−∫q_u dμ), over actual relative E¹ metrics. If μ(P)>0, the objective of F(w) is infinite. Finite dual energy therefore forces μ(P)=0 before lifting the target.

The needed topological inverse has a complete proof. Let p:S→T be a continuous surjection of compact Hausdorff spaces, C closed, F=p⁻¹(C), and let j:T\C→S\F invert a complement homeomorphism. For finite Radon μ with μ(C)=0, Λ(g)=∫_{T\C}g(j(x))dμ is a positive bounded functional on C(S). Riesz gives Radon ν. Continuous tests give p_*ν=μ. For compact K⊂T\C, normality gives 0≤g≤1 supported off F and equal to one on p⁻¹K. Then ν(S\F)≥Λ(g)≥μ(K); inner regularity proves ν(F)=0. For compact K′ off F, p⁻¹(p(K′))=K′, so its measure is determined. Inner regularity proves uniqueness, and simple functions plus monotone convergence identify all Borel and upper-bounded extended integrals. No metric-space or countable-exhaustion assumption occurs.

Apply this with C=P^an and F=D^an. Off the zero-mass sets, q_{F(ψ)} is the actual ψ through the isomorphism. Hence ∫q_u dμ=∫ψ dν and D_M(μ)=E_raw,A^∨(ν). The exact ample grant gives finite D_M precisely when EVERY actual relative E¹ quotient q_u is integrable. Conversely, all-quotient integrability first excludes P through w and then gives the same ample equivalence. The absolute singular original u is not asserted integrable. Granted mixed-test integrability of w also makes every transferred mixed output give P zero mass.
